claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x, the parallel batched Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md (P=4096 walks sharing one r=64 transition table with per-walk coefficient offsets, Montgomery-batched additions, shared distinguished-point table) succeeds with probability at least 0.3995 using at most 2^128.146 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^105.59 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^24 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps, or random-oracle premises. Success relies on the supported shared-function random-mapping and hash-bucket heuristics, disclosed and supported in proof.md; non-degeneracy holds by integer-range layout. This is an analytic best-known-attack cost analysis, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical multi-walk attack path on the fixed prime-order toy curve (n=9883) and measure success rate against the birthday prediction. This does not establish production curve behavior or cost bounds.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: parallel batched rho, r=64, segmented table, at 39%+ success
